author: sjm41
body:
* **ARBA rule (ID and label):**
ARBA00027533

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
Dmel wal (Q7KN94)

* **Description of issue**
Dmel wal (Q7KN94) is an Electron transfer flavoprotein subunit alpha, so not an enzyme.

But it gets 'catalytic activity' via ARBA:ARBA00027533
I thinks that's because it fulfils this statement:

IF
InterPro signature:`IPR029035`
taxon: Ephydroidea
THEN
GO term [GO:0003824](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/term/GO:0003824)

But IPR029035 is the high-level homologous superfamily 'DHS-like NAD/FAD-binding domain superfamily', that covers various enzymes as well as electron transfer protein subunits. Its presence alone is not sufficient to give a 'catalytic activity' annotation, so I think this statement should be removed from this ARBA rule.
title: ARBA00027533

author: Antonialock
body:
This protein has exactly the same interpro and funfams as the human ETFA protein, so it is a very strange rule (to apply the annotation to Ephydroidea entries with this interpro).

I am curating this entry for swiss-prot - that should make the condition disappear from the ARBA and I will put this on my list of "very strange taxon constraints".

I managed to add in vitro/IDA evidence for electron transfer activity from PMID: 22580358, I think I can also add fatty acid beta-oxidation since they used octanoyl-CoA+MCAD in the assay. This was nice to see since I think we only had examples of the MF/BP from human previously. 

I also cleaned up human annotation, removing oxidoreductase GO annotation and uniprot COFACTOR topics and some other bits and bobs.
